items.claim: Two Hebrew quotes are glossed with a span wider than the word(s) actually quoted, borrowing sense from unquoted neighboring words.
items.evidence: The row quotes only כִּֽי תֵ֭שֵׁב ('when you sit') but glosses it 'when you sit to eat with a ruler,' which is the sense of the full clause כִּֽי תֵ֭שֵׁב לִלְח֣וֹם אֶת מוֹשֵׁ֑ל (oshb:Prov.23.1); it also quotes only כְּזָבִֽים ('lies/falsehoods') but glosses it 'deceptive food,' a sense that belongs to the two-word phrase לֶ֣חֶם כְּזָבִֽים (oshb:Prov.23.3), not to the quoted word alone. The span argument itself (protasis at 23:1, prohibition-plus-motive at 23:3, petuchah/pe closing the immediately preceding verse) is sound and not in question.

items.claim: The petuchah and ketiv/qere citations are correctly counted and the topic break from the ruler's table is real.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json lists PE at Prov.23.5 (closing this row's span) and 2 ketiv/qere notes at Prov.23.5, matching the row's 'pair, both verbs' claim; the Hebrew quote is same-span with its gloss; no content token links Prov.23.3's food/deceit language to Prov.23.4's wealth-and-restraint language.

items.claim: Two Hebrew quotes are glossed with a span wider than the word(s) actually quoted.
items.evidence: אַל תִּלְחַ֗ם ('do not eat') is glossed 'do not eat the bread of a stingy-eyed man,' the sense of the full clause אַל תִּלְחַ֗ם אֶת לֶ֭חֶם רַ֣ע עָ֑יִן (oshb:Prov.23.6); כִּ֤י ('for') is glossed 'for as he reckons the cost, so he is,' the sense of the full clause כִּ֤י כְּמוֹ שָׁעַ֥ר בְּנַפְשׁ֗וֹ כֶּ֫ן ה֥וּא (oshb:Prov.23.7). The petuchah/ketiv-qere citations at 23:5-6 are otherwise correctly counted, and the boundary reasoning against merging with the 23:1-3 table scene (distinct hosts, no catchword bridge) is sound.
tier_citations: tier-3 (pmarks_Prov.json, PE Prov.23.5 / kq Prov.23.6, single-witness)

items.claim: The verse's second Hebrew quote is glossed with a span wider than the word actually quoted.
items.evidence: כִּֽי ('for') is glossed 'for he will despise the wisdom of your words,' the sense of the full clause כִּֽי יָ֝ב֗וּז לְשֵׂ֣כֶל מִלֶּֽיךָ (oshb:Prov.23.9); the row's first quote is correctly same-span with its gloss. The admonition_unit-vs-single_proverb call for this one-verse imperative-plus-motive unit is a defensible reading, honestly self-flagged at medium confidence.

items.claim: The repeated boundary-stone phrase and the four-verse gap back to Prov.22.28 are both byte-confirmed, and the rejected merge is the right rival to reject.
items.evidence: אַל תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם (oshb:Prov.22.28) and אַל תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם (oshb:Prov.23.10) are byte-identical including accents; three intervening scenes (ruler's table, wealth-that-vanishes, stingy host) sit between them, supporting restatement over an uninterrupted span. The verse-11 quote is same-span with its gloss.

items.claim: Isolating Prov.23.12 as a standalone attention-formula verse is undercut by a stronger catchword rival than the row credits, and by the row's own analogy.
items.evidence: לַמּוּסָ֣ר closes this verse ('...heart to musar') and מוּסָ֑ר opens the very next verse's prohibition ('do not withhold musar from a child') — word-adjacent repetition straddling this row's own right seam, a materially stronger link than the 'one repeated root' the rejected_alternative dismisses it as. The row's device_notes compares Prov.23.12's function to Prov.22.17, but Prov.22.17 is not itself an isolated row: it is the opening verse of the Prov.22.17-21 prologue unit. The same analogy argues Prov.23.12 more plausibly opens a Prov.23.12-14 general-then-specific unit (general call to heed musar, then the child-discipline case) than that it stands alone.

items.claim: The row's own left seam carries an undisclosed catchword tie to Prov.23.12, and the rejected_alternative answers a weaker rival than that one.
items.evidence: מוּסָ֑ר is the operative noun opening this row's own prohibition at Prov.23.13, repeating לַמּוּסָ֣ר at the close of the immediately preceding verse, Prov.23.12 — a byte-true device straddling this row's left seam that is named in neither the rationale nor boundary_evidence_refs. The rejected_alternative answers a weaker rival (splitting Prov.23.14 off as its own single_proverb) rather than the stronger one (extending the unit left to include Prov.23.12 as its general premise).

items.claim: The vocative and both edge boundaries are byte-clean: correctly placed among the isolated bni occurrences and unlinked by catchword to either neighbor.
items.evidence: Prov.23.15's vocative matches the isolated bni-vocative occurrences (Prov.23.15 and Prov.23.19 both listed, distinct from the chs.1-7 lecture-frame cluster); no content token bridges Prov.23.14's Sheol-language close to Prov.23.15's vocative opening, nor Prov.23.16's close to Prov.23.17's fear-Yahweh opening.
